To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incidence of lung metastases in rats with HCC induced by ciprofibrate increased with time, and all the lung metastases were negative for gamma-glutamyal transpeptidase (GCT) activity.
the liver tumors induced by peroxisome profilers have a high incidence of metastatic potential.

1) the incidence of lung metastases in rats with hepatomas induced by cipofibrate increased with time, 2) the metastatic lesions were multifocal and located in blood vessels and parenchyama, 3) all the metastatic floci examined for GGT expression were devoid of GGT, and 4) these findings demonstrate the malignant behavior and the phenotypic property of ciprofibrated-induced liver tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of liver tumors in rats by a peroxisomal proliferator, ciprofibrate and the characterization of the tumors induced.
the induction of hepatocellular carcinogenesis in rats by ciprofibrates and the development of metastatic disease in the lungs.
the development of new drugs to treat cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incidence and behavior of ciprofibrate-induced HCC in rats is similar to that of HCC induced by other peroxisome profilers.
peroxisome proliferation is a multistage process and that the liver tumor induced by peroxisome profilers is not benign but malignant.
the liver tumors induced by ciprofbirrate are malignant, but the absence of GCT expression in metastases does not appear to be a general feature in all peroxisome-proliferator-induced liver tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the liver tumors induced by peroxisome profilers, such as ciprofibrate and Wy 14643, are highly malignant and metastasize to lungs in a significant percentage of animals, but the expression of the GGT is absent in these metastatic tumors.

the absence of GGG expression in the metastases of HCC induced by peroxisome profilers is a characteristic of these tumors and that the absence of the enzyme in the metastases is not related to the absence in the primary tumors.

ciprofibrate is a potent carcinogen and that the absence of GCT activity in metastatic lesions is not due to the loss of the gene encoding this enzyme but rather is a phenotypic characteristic of the primary HCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peroxisome proliferation is a risk factor for the development of HCC and that these tumors can metastasize.
ciprofibrate is a potent carcinogen and the liver tumors induced by this agent have a high metastatic potential and that metastases do not express GGT.

peroxisome proliferation does not seem to be a prerequisite for the development of liver tumors and their metastasis, but rather a peroxisomal proliferator may act as a promoter for liver carcinogenesis.
